content:
Lina: quick heads-up 10: telemetry shows rerank dashboard buckets jumping after yesterday's deploy. looks correlated with collector packing. anyone seen the same?
Raj: yep. runtime emits float scores but collector serializes to compact int to save bytes. quantization is moving bucket boundaries.
Miguel: we chose packing for throughput; surprised it affected quota math.
Sara: product risk: noisy SLA alerts and confusing regressions in console. customers will blame model changes.
Kevin: quota uses score_units = ceil(score * weight). small quantization leads to different throttle outcomes for same candidate set.
Lina: proposals: 1) keep packed ints but publish exact decoder & bucket map; 2) stop packing and emit float end-to-end; 3) emit per-model histograms for dashboards only. quick pros/cons?
Raj: (1) fastest, brittle across versions. (2) simplest semantics, ~12% bandwidth cost. (3) good for dashboards but loses candidate-level debugging.
Miguel: bandwidth impact measurable but acceptable if we gzip and sample traces.
Sara: rollout UX: per-tenant opt-in and console toggle to view "legacy" vs "canonical" buckets; show distribution preview per model in rollout flow.
Lina: implementation idea: collector emits both fields during a transition window: score_float and score_q16 (legacy). router prefers score_float when present; fallback to decode q16.
Raj: I'll add fallback decode and tests.
Kevin: gate with 5% tenants canary. SLO: <=2% change in 95th throttle rate and no significant uptick in alerts. I'll build a side-by-side metric.
deploy-bot: started canary: rerank-collector/v2 on cluster rerank-canary (pods=3). mem < 70%, p50 latency +2ms.
Lina: action items: Miguel -> dual-field collector canary; Raj -> router fallback + unit/integration tests; Kevin -> SLO + comparison dashboard; Sara -> console toggle + copy; Lina -> coordinate rollout notes and platform announcement. reconvene after 48h of canary data. :thumbsup:
